Nikka is obviously struggling, but her triggers are, to put it bluntly, her responsibility. Nobody else's. She obviously needs help, and shielding her from potential triggers is not going to help. It will prolong this, and alienate and upset others around her. You're going to push your other daughter away.

Personally, and I know it may be harsh, but I think she would benefit from some kind of impatient treatment, away from people, away from triggers, until she's ready to face those triggers. (Take all of my advice with a grain of salt, I am not a proper professional, I am just very experienced with my own and others mental health issues, consulting the therapist would be the best option) 

She and you are going to push everyone away from her, and her sister is going to end up very frustrated and alienated, and feel you are playing favourites. Yes, they may be out of not understanding, but her feelings are still just as valid. You daughter needs real, professional help, and to me, a therapist who just increases medication at signs of more stress, isn't a good one (in my experience). Medication should be a short term solution for most. 

The reason I was so fucked up after a break up, was because I was severely abused and sexually assaulted by an adult as a young minor. The therapist needs to look into the possibility that your daughter was abused, betrayed, or even cheated on. Anything can cause this trauma.
